Analysis tests the main effect of similarity (Different > Similar) at outcome when participants observe others' choices relative to their own — a social preference-learning task assessing social processing. Global criteria for healthy adult whole-brain group maps are met and the contrast measures social processing.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). However, the analysis does not assess affiliation or attachment (no measures of bonding/close relationships or contrasts like loved one vs stranger); AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not satisfied.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). The task probes learning about preference similarity rather than communication (reception/production of facial or non-facial signals); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not satisfied.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). The contrast concerns others' choices relative to the participant (preference similarity) and models learning about others rather than explicit self-evaluation or self-knowledge; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not satisfied.

Analysis measures how participants represent others' preferences (similar vs different) — directly indexing perception/understanding of others' traits/choices. Global whole-brain criteria are met and local criteria for perception of others apply.

Conjunction of AS and PE parametric modulators in the similarity GLM indexes social learning about agreement/similarity between self and others at outcome — a social processing measure. Global whole-brain criteria are met.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). The analysis focuses on preference-similarity prediction signals rather than affiliation/attachment constructs; AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 are not satisfied.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). The analysis models similarity-related learning signals, not social communication (facial or non-facial reception/production); SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not satisfied.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). Although similarity is computed relative to the self, the analysis targets learning about others' agreement/PE signals rather than explicit self-evaluation or self-knowledge measures; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not satisfied.

The conjunction of AS and PE in the similarity GLM reflects neural signals for perceiving and learning about others' choices relative to the participant — meeting perception-of-others criteria. Global whole-brain criteria are met.
Positive AC ASim ∩ ADiff (consistency GLM conjunction) indexes social inference about agents' similarity/consistency — a social processing measure. Global whole-brain criteria are satisfied.

Global criteria are met (GLOBAL_I1, GLOBAL_I2). This consistency GLM addresses learning about others' behavior, not communication processes; SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2 are not satisfied.
